title: A Safe Sleep Space for Baby
hook: Pediatric guidance for safer infant sleep is simple: a firm, flat surface with nothing in it — no pillows, blankets, bumpers, or soft toys.
key_points: Use a firm, flat sleep surface (crib, bassinet, or play yard) that meets current safety standards.
Keep the space bare: no soft bedding, pillows, crib bumpers, or stuffed animals near a sleeping baby.
Room-sharing without bed-sharing — baby in their own crib in the parents' room — is recommended for at least the first 6 months.
Avoid overheating; dress the baby in light layers and skip loose blankets, using a sleep sack if needed.
content_html: Where a baby sleeps matters as much as how you lay them down. The pediatric advice for a safer sleep space is reassuringly minimalist: a firm, flat surface — a crib, bassinet, or play yard meeting current safety standards — with nothing else in it.
extra_html: That means no pillows, no loose blankets, no crib bumpers, and no stuffed animals near a sleeping baby, all of which raise the risk of suffocation. The AAP also recommends room-sharing without bed-sharing for at least the first six months: the baby sleeps in their own crib in the parents' room, not in the adult bed. To avoid overheating, dress the baby in light layers and use a wearable sleep sack rather than loose covers. This is general guidance; your pediatrician can help with specific questions about your baby's sleep.

related.title: Always Put a Baby to Sleep on Their Back
related.hook: Placing healthy babies on their back for every sleep — naps and night — is the single most effective step to reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS).

related.title: A Smoke-Free World Is Safer for Babies
related.hook: Keeping a baby away from smoke is one of the few SIDS risk factors parents fully control — and it also means fewer chest infections, ear infections, and asthma flare-ups.

flashcards.prompt: What belongs in a safe infant sleep space?

choices.text: Nothing but the baby on a firm, flat surface
A soft pillow and a cozy blanket
Crib bumpers and a few stuffed animals

flashcards.explanation_html: A firm, flat, bare surface lowers suffocation and SIDS risk. Soft bedding, pillows, bumpers, and toys should be kept out of the sleep space.

flashcards.prompt: What sleep arrangement does the AAP recommend for at least the first 6 months?
flashcards.back_html: Room-sharing without bed-sharing — the baby sleeps in their own crib or bassinet in the parents' room, not in the adult bed.

flashcards.prompt: How should you keep a baby from overheating during sleep?

choices.text: Light layers and a sleep sack instead of loose blankets
A thick duvet tucked in tightly
A warm hat indoors at all times

flashcards.explanation_html: Loose blankets are a hazard and overheating raises risk. Light layers or a wearable sleep sack keep the baby warm without loose bedding.
